item.subject: maths
item.stem: The diagram shows isosceles triangle PQR with $PR = QR$ and midpoint M of base PQ. Rohan has already shown $\triangle PRM \cong \triangle QRM$.

parts.text: Which claim correctly uses that congruence?

options.text: Corresponding parts are equal, so $\angle PRM = \angle QRM$.
Equal angles at R are what create the congruence of $\triangle PRM$ and $\triangle QRM$.
Congruence applies to every triangle pair in the figure, including ones that were not matched.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.
